statement: On 8 real bug-fix tasks, accuracy was the same with and without the harness, and after a fix to its permission settings cost showed no measurable difference either. A first run found it cost more because its own permission settings refused 35 ordinary calls; after a fix, cost per solved task is $0.0935 against $0.0917 for /init and $0.0827 for no instruction file; the paired per-task difference shows no clear difference against either. Accuracy was equal.

pipeline.source: bench/value/PROTOCOL-v2.md and the bench/value/ files named per step; text from the facts sheet block how_it_works

steps.title: Tasks by rule
steps.what_happens: Tasks are merged pull requests from public MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0 repositories in Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, merged after 2026-06-30, newest first. The pull request must close a linked issue in the same repository with a prose description (at least 20 words, issue at most 365 days old), change at most 3 non-test files and 100 non-test lines, add or change at least one test file, and touch no dependency manifest. Each candidate is validated in Docker with no network: target tests fail at the base commit with the test patch applied and pass with the real fix, 3 of 3 times each, within 300 s. Result: the 5 pilot tasks (click x2, flask, attrs, express) plus 3 held-out tasks, all from pallets/werkzeug. The rule aimed for 5 held-out tasks and found 3 (the minimum allowed).
steps.controls: Nobody picks a task by hand. Every rejected candidate is recorded with its reason (1,877 rows in rejected-v2.jsonl). The manifest is frozen with a checksum (c8bde114...) before any paid run. The repository stores references only: URLs, commit SHAs and the SHA-256 of the issue text.

steps.title: Base commit only
steps.what_happens: materialize.py rebuilds each task in a scratch directory from the manifest: issue.md (re-fetched and checked against issue_sha256), test.patch, gold.patch and repo/ (the tree at base_sha, the commit before the fix). For the generator, a fresh local git repository is built per task holding only base_sha and its ancestors: branch main only, no tags, no remote, reflogs expired, unreachable objects pruned.
steps.controls: A check before the arm is accepted: HEAD equals base_sha; the fix commit and every pull-request commit are absent; no exported file contains the fix SHA, a PR commit SHA (full or 12-character prefix) or the PR number as #NNNN. A failure stops the benchmark.

steps.title: Three setups
steps.what_happens: none: the repository at the base commit, no instruction file. generic: the same plus a CLAUDE.md written by Claude Code's own /init at that commit, through the meter (cost $0.4557 for 8 tasks, reported separately as setup). olivium: the same plus the unmodified output of `bin/harnessforge generate PATH --runtime claude_code --export DIR --json`: CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json, the hook scripts under .claude/hooks/ and .olivium/*. The generator parses repository files and git history, runs nothing from the repository and calls no model (setup $0).
steps.controls: Every setup starts from the same snapshot. entry.sh first removes any CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, copilot-instructions.md, .claude or .cursor shipped with the repository, at any depth. Before the agent starts it records the SHA-256 of every harness file and of the --settings file; the runner compares them with the arm's files and scores the trial infra_error on any mismatch.

steps.title: One container per run
steps.what_happens: Each run is one headless Claude Code 2.1.311 session (`claude -p --output-format stream-json`) with model claude-sonnet-5-5 in its own Docker container, created from a per-task image, files copied in with docker cp, no host mounts. Limits: 60 main-session turns, 1200 s (20 minutes), $3 per run; container limits 1500m memory, 2 CPUs, 512 processes. The container is on an internal Docker network whose only peer is the meter; it holds a dummy API key. The prompt is the issue title and body followed by 'Fix this issue in the repository in the current directory.'
steps.controls: Same image, prompt, model, limits and UV_NO_SYNC=1 in every setup. WebSearch and WebFetch are removed in every setup and in /init (--disallowedTools), because a search runs on the API side, past the container's isolation, and could find the upstream fix. Permission modes differ on purpose: none and generic run with bypassPermissions and one shared benchmark settings file; olivium runs its exported settings byte for byte (--settings) in default mode with no bypass, so a call its own rules refuse counts against it.
steps.ref: claude -p --output-format stream-json (the Olivium setup adds --settings with its exported file)

steps.title: Metering proxy
steps.what_happens: The meter is a reverse proxy to the Anthropic Messages API. It alone holds the API key, injects it when forwarding, attributes each request to its run id (/run/<run_id>/...), reads token usage from the API responses and prices it from a price table (claude-sonnet-5-5: $2 input, $10 output, $2.50 5-minute cache write, $0.10 cache read per million tokens). It enforces a per-run cap and a total cap and appends every request to requests.jsonl. The default mode is a mock model that contacts no API.
steps.controls: Fail-closed: an unknown model, an unwritable log or a 200 response without readable usage stops forwarding. With --refuse-web-tools it refuses any request that offers a web search or fetch server tool. The log never holds headers, bodies or the key. In the first run the meter's cost equalled Claude Code's own total_cost_usd on every trial (0 mismatches above one millionth); 501 meter rows, all live, none offering a web or server tool.

steps.title: Hidden tests
steps.what_happens: The agent's patch is extracted (excluding CLAUDE.md, .claude/ and .olivium/) and applied to a clean checkout at the base commit in a fresh container started with --network none. Every test file, test configuration, lint configuration and CI file the agent touched is then restored or removed, the real test patch from the pull request is applied, and lint and the tests run. Solved means every fail-to-pass test passes and no pass-to-pass test regresses; the repository's linter result is recorded separately.
steps.controls: The agent never sees the real test patch. Restoring test files and configuration means an agent cannot pass by weakening the tests; root-level modules that could shadow the test runner are also restored. A run that hits a limit is scored unsolved and its cost counts. Stated gap: forgery through ordinary source files in the package under test is not detected.
sources: change log 'Grading also restores test configuration', 'Grading also removes test-runner shadows')

steps.title: Paired by task
steps.what_happens: Three questions: fewer tokens and lower cost; better context (files read outside the real fix, turns and tool calls before the first edit to a file the real fix changed); more accurate (solved, regressions, lint). For each task the 3 repeats of each setup are averaged. The difference is olivium minus the other setup for that task. The headline is the median of those differences across tasks, with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval: tasks resampled with replacement 10,000 times, seed 20261108. Cost per solved task is the setup's total cost divided by its solved runs and has no interval.
steps.controls: An interval that includes zero is reported as no clear difference. Held-out tasks are also reported separately. Every report section carries the line: '8 tasks, one model, one agent. This can show a direction or a problem. It cannot prove a general effect.' Numbers reach other documents only from results.json.

steps.title: Whatever it shows
steps.what_happens: Under docs/benchmarks: report.md, results.json, charts, per-trial summaries (trace, grade, state, harness check, meter rows), the meter log, the schedule and provenance.json with commands, digests, spend and checksums.
steps.controls: No third-party source, issue text, test patches, agent patches or transcripts are published; refused commands in the first run are cut to their leading program words and paths. Mock output is stamped REHEARSAL and stays in the scratch directory.

before_the_steps.title: Pre-registration
before_the_steps.what_happens: The design (setups, task rule, limits, metrics, analysis, stop rules) was written in PROTOCOL-v2.md on 2026-11-09, after the pilot and before held-out task selection, rehearsal or any scored run of this version; the 5 pilot tasks were carried over unchanged. Every later change is a dated change-log entry with its reason, and the file's SHA-256 at each state is appended to PROTOCOL-v2.sha256 (6 states). The first scored run used state 90bbbacc... (2026-11-10T09:56:42Z); the after-fix re-run was written into the change log at state 376b8a64... (2026-11-10T12:01:33Z) before it ran (run window 12:11 to 12:31 UTC).
before_the_steps.controls: Nothing in the first scored run was chosen from its outcome data. The after-fix re-run was decided after that outcome and logged before it ran. The result is published whatever it is. If a benchmark bug is found after scored runs begin, all scored runs are discarded and repeated; runs are never re-done selectively.

schedule.title: Schedule and repeats
schedule.what_happens: 8 tasks x 3 setups x 3 repeats = 72 scored runs. The order is shuffled with seed 20261108 so time of day and prompt-cache warmth are spread across setups. Two runs go at a time. Before the scored run, a paid canary (one task, three setups, one repeat) runs in its own directory and is never scored.
schedule.controls: A run that ends as infra_error (API outage, Docker failure, harness-check mismatch, a web tool offered) is left out of the scores and repeated, up to 3 attempts; a run that fails because of the model or the harness is never repeated. In the first run: 72 scheduled, 72 completed, 0 retries, 0 timeouts, 0 turn limits, 0 budget_exhausted, 0 infra errors.

limits.source: Texts from the facts sheet block limits; each item names its own published source

items.text: 8 tasks, one model (claude-sonnet-5-5), one agent (Claude Code 2.1.311). This can show a direction or a problem. It cannot prove a general effect.
The after-fix run uses the same tasks the fix was found on, so it is not a held-out result.
After-fix comparison uses setups from two runs a few hours apart: none and /init are the first run's runs, not re-run.
Accuracy could not move in either direction on this task set: each task was solved by all its runs or by none (5 always, 3 never), in every setup.

The analyzer and rule filters were tuned while looking at pallets/click, pallets/flask, python-attrs/attrs and expressjs/express at the same base commits; the 5 pilot tasks come from those repositories. Only the held-out table is free of that overlap.
items.source: docs/benchmarks/value-v2-2026-11-09/report.md 'Read this first: overlap with the tuning repositories'

items.text: All 3 held-out tasks come from one repository, pallets/werkzeug, which shares an owner and likely layout and tooling conventions with tuned repositories. The held-out table is free of the base-commit overlap but not of that family resemblance. The rule aimed for 5 held-out tasks and found 3.

Bug fixes only, two languages (7 Python tasks, 1 JavaScript); held-out tasks are Python only. Extra repositories had to fit one generic uv install recipe, a limit of the benchmark's install machinery.

The baselines run with permission checks bypassed and the harness runs with its own permissions in default mode. That is the pre-registered design (the harness is measured as exported), so refusals count against the harness only.
'Files read outside the real fix' is a lower bound: reads through grep, rg, find or interpreters are not counted.
items.source: bench/value/PROTOCOL.md change log 'Trace limitation, stated plainly'

items.text: The pilot (2026-11-09, 5 tasks, 45 runs) measured an older harness with exported settings not used and web tools offered. Its numbers are a different run with a different harness and do not form a before/after comparison.
The generated permissions are a filter, not a sandbox: an allowed interpreter or runner can do anything the user can. Run unattended sessions in a container or VM.

items.text: The harness was already changed once before the first run. A paid canary on click #3858 found 5 refused calls; the generator's allow list was widened and the guard hook added before any scored run. The canary is not scored.
